profile.name: Avery Freeman
profile.positioning: Systems-minded software builder connecting AI tools, infrastructure, data, business operations, and human workflows.
profile.target_context: AI software development and adjacent product engineering roles
profile.summary: Combines current self-directed work on agent workflows and developer tools with hands-on systems consulting, software and data projects, AV operations, business study, and client-facing team work.

top_ten.skill: Turn human needs into buildable scope
top_ten.claim: Connects a specific user need to product behavior, technical choices, and useful limits.
boundaries: Use project and coursework evidence; do not claim user counts, election outcomes, or measured impact without a source.

top_ten.skill: Design architecture teams can carry forward
top_ten.claim: Creates durable project context, architecture records, workflow rules, and validation paths for coding-agent projects.
boundaries: Git-BBQ is the direct public project example. Do not infer sole authorship of related repositories whose README credits another maintainer.

top_ten.claim: Explores explicit task state, checkpoints, verification, recovery, and human control across work that spans multiple steps.
boundaries: Describe as project work; do not imply enterprise-scale deployment.

top_ten.skill: Connect AI tools to real systems
top_ten.claim: Builds or adapts tool interfaces that connect coding assistants with operating-system and browser workflows.
boundaries: codex-mcp-for-ubuntu is a fork adapted to Codex; describe the repair and adaptation, not original authorship of its upstream code.

top_ten.skill: Build software across languages and layers
top_ten.claim: Has public project examples spanning Go, Python, Rust, TypeScript, and application, service, CLI, and tool-integration surfaces.
boundaries: Projects establish hands-on breadth; they do not establish equal depth in every language.

top_ten.claim: Builds data workflows and communicates analysis through validated publishing steps, maps, and charts.
boundaries: The geospatial project supports analysis and visualization claims; do not claim policy impact.

top_ten.skill: Work across application and infrastructure boundaries
top_ten.claim: Connects application behavior, external APIs, operating systems, networks, storage, and deployment constraints.
boundaries: Public repositories show project architecture; infrastructure experience is owner-reported professional work.

top_ten.skill: Troubleshoot with reliability and security controls in view
top_ten.claim: Combines dependency repair and explicit tool permissions in software projects with operational infrastructure and PCI/DSS experience.
boundaries: PCI/DSS experience is owner-reported implementation and self-assessment work, not QSA certification or a security-audit credential.

top_ten.skill: Model business processes and practical value
top_ten.claim: Connects process design, staffing, scheduling, equipment, billing, pricing assumptions, and delivery requirements.
boundaries: The AV rental estimate is potential annual revenue modeled from assumptions; it is not realized revenue. Scheduling savings are owner-reported.

top_ten.claim: Writes practical procedures and guides, trains staff, coordinates customer-facing delivery, and adapts explanations to the audience.
boundaries: Prefer examples of a guide, training material, or audience adaptation over generic communication claims.

career_timeline.milestone: Early computer and audio interests; owner-authored summary says first desktop PC was assembled at age eight.
career_timeline.scope_note: Personal origin context; not professional experience at that age.

career_timeline.milestone: Studied liberal arts with an audio-engineering and electronic-music composition focus at The Evergreen State College.
Early campus IT support included workstation migration and Exchange transition tasks, according to the archival timeline.
career_timeline.scope_note: Owner-reported archival timeline; keep distinct from later formal programming study.

career_timeline.milestone: Worked as an executive language consultant in Tokyo, adapting financial and economic explanations for multinational business audiences.
Completed MBA study in Management, including operations, marketing research, econometrics, and finance coursework.
Completed marketing-research and software-adoption analysis work, then additional accounting, SQL, data-architecture, Excel, and SAS study.
Owner-reported IT systems consulting across POS and payment systems, wireless, surveillance, virtualization, storage, remote access, controls, and automation.
career_timeline.scope_note: Dates and outcomes are owner-reported professional records.

career_timeline.milestone: On-call banquet and event work involving event-order interpretation, staff coordination, customer needs, and changing delivery requirements.
Completed Full Stack JavaScript Web + Mobile Development coursework.
Hotel banquet management and AV segment work included equipment and rate planning, billing, scheduling, inventory, procedures, and staff instruction.
career_timeline.scope_note: The $45,000 annual rental figure was a modeled potential based on $150 average rental/event × 25 events/month × 12; the 3–8 hours/week scheduling reduction is owner-reported.

career_timeline.milestone: Completed backend, SQL, and DevOps with Python coursework; the geospatial project is identified as an honors project.
Licensed process-service work and high-touch club dining keep careful procedure, trust, and reliable customer service part of current day-to-day work.
career_timeline.scope_note: Include as current human-facing operational experience; omit client identities, case details, and other private information.

career_timeline.milestone: Current public project and writing activity includes developer-agent workflows, MCP integrations, architecture context, and automation.
career_timeline.scope_note: Current self-directed AI development practice; no reviewed evidence of prior production AI employment.

claim_boundaries: Describe AI and agent-tool work as current self-directed practice, not prior production AI employment.
Describe the Mayflower Park $45,000 figure as modeled potential annual revenue based on stated assumptions; do not claim it was realized.
Keep the reported 3–8 hours per week scheduling reduction attributed to owner records, not independent measurement.
Keep coursework and honors projects distinct from paid production software work.
Describe PCI/DSS work as owner-reported implementation and self-assessment experience, not QSA certification or a security-audit credential.
Describe codex-mcp-for-ubuntu as a fork repaired and adapted for Codex; do not claim authorship of upstream code.
Do not infer sole authorship of related repositories whose README credits another maintainer.
Do not publish contact details, private file names or paths, reference information, background or credit-check material, signatures, or third-party personal information.
